agent_priors_used: PRIOR (general caching-systems knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): a cache or compiled artifact pays for itself only when the reuse count exceeds a break-even that depends on the cost of RE-VALIDATING the cached item, not of producing it. Systems that re-validate cheaply amortize; systems that must re-derive do not. Used to judge that SPIDER's 48.00-versus-38.6 cost separation is a statement about the ledger's re-derivation price as much as about memory.

PRIOR (general tool-agent knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): in long-horizon tool use the dominant failure mode is compounding error across steps, so mechanisms that remove steps compound in value - but a mechanism that silently replays a wrong action injects error at the same rate it removes work. Used to weight the synthetic 80 false compiled replays as an architectural liability rather than a bookkeeping detail, and to justify requiring a null arm that omits gating identity on any replay mechanism.

PRIOR (general measurement knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): an instrument used to adjudicate a cost or economics question must first be calibrated on cases whose correct answer is known by construction, and a battery of constant statistics calibrates nothing. Used to accept physics' diagnosis of its own frozen accept branch and to reject any third certification cycle that repeats it.

PRIOR (general research-system knowledge, not SPIDER evidence): capability that exists only in an uncommitted working tree across many experiment cycles has near-zero expected value, and re-measuring against a moving artifact produces incomparable numbers. Used to make durable commitment at HEAD a binding precondition of the product mandate rather than an auxiliary check.

PRIOR (general research knowledge about fast-moving fields, not SPIDER evidence): external numeric comparators are frequently absent, and an honest, bounded 'no comparator exists' produced cheaply is itself decision-grade because it stops the program spending cycles trying to match a phantom. Used to authorise intel's external-transfer question with a negative as a first-class outcome.

PRIOR (general knowledge about experimental design, not SPIDER evidence): the cheapest sufficient substrate should be preferred until a question genuinely requires a more expensive one. Plain credential-free public HTTP has now been shown inside SPIDER to support 155 real observations with paired bootstrap CIs, so questions about architectural preconditions should be moved onto it before anyone pays for a browser or a model key. Used to put frontier's mandate on real sites with no browser, docker or model key.

PRIOR (general knowledge about human and agentic computer use, not SPIDER evidence - asserted here only as a question, and explicitly handed to intel to measure rather than to assume): the delegable or recurrent fraction of activity in computer use is a minority, not a majority, and the overhead ratio paid for re-deriving that minority is large. The Scout supplied concrete figures for this (R = 60-343x, delegable recurrence h = 7.7-9 percent) from a source SPIDER has never verified. If true, h would bound the entire reachable economic share of SPIDER's product regardless of how good inheritance is, which is why I directed intel to verify or refute it rather than treating it as background.

PRIOR (general knowledge about measurement and research operations, not SPIDER evidence): when a local result is negative-leaning, the first question is whether the instrument or the ledger is at fault before generalising, and the second is to search for the setting in which the mechanism could still win. Used to require product to declare one cost basis and one break-even derivation, and to keep the amortization question alive on a substrate with genuine cold-discovery cost instead of abandoning it on a substrate with none.

allocation.question: Leaving the synthetic plan family entirely: on real, credential-free, publicly reachable websites with a true holdout and no site-identity leakage - mechanisms learned on a TRAIN set of sites, executed only on TEST sites never observed during distillation, with the site-identity signal provably absent from every inherited mechanism - three things are measured. (1) IS THE ARCHITECTURAL PRECONDITION PRESENT ON THE REAL WEB? What fraction of real action-gating objects expose a STABLE, agent-visible, episode-invariant identifier - a canonical resource id, a self-describing URL, a stable link relation, a stable ETag, a session-independent handle - readable in the response, equal across episodes, and sufficient together with the observable state to determine the declared action; and what is the matching fraction for the session-scoped identifiers (CSRF-bound-to-session, rotating capability handles) that cannot support cross-episode replay. (2) DOES INHERITED, PARAMETERIZED TRANSFER ACTUALLY EXECUTE ON A HELD-OUT SITE - resolving to the correct action and verifying against a response-derived postcondition, at what rate, with what abstention rate, and with what honest cost in real tokens, requests, verification and repair? (3) DOES IT AMORTIZE? Does the inherited arm cost less than cold re-exploration AND less than a no-memory deterministic executor that re-derives every episode, on this real substrate, rather than on an abstract ledger with no token mapping. MANDATORY NULL ARM: a mechanism whose replay key omits the gating object's identity - which is exactly the shape of SPIDER's own state-keyed cache - which must produce silently wrong actions at a measurable rate, converting the synthetic 80-of-600 false-compiled-replay finding into a real, credential-free number. Mandatory honest control: minimal structural observation representation (the 763-token representation already established on real sites) so that the amortization question is not answered by throwing away the 68x. No browser, no docker, no model key, no network beyond the public sites themselves, no LLM calls; arms are deterministic policies so the measurement is an upper bound on information available to any policy, labelled as such. Falsifier and architecture consequence, declared before freeze: if stable agent-visible identifiers are absent or rare on real sites, then NO sound cross-episode action-replay cache is viable in SPIDER's target domain, the residual must be paid by per-episode re-derivation, and the synthetic evidence that re-derivation is CHEAPER (38.6 units versus 48.0) then becomes the operative design fact - SPIDER's persistent-replay architecture is re-specified or dropped, and that is a valid, valuable, decisive negative. If stable identifiers are present and the inherited arm amortizes on held-out sites, the architecture is retained but re-specified on measured evidence rather than on a planted one.
allocation.rationale: Frontier is the lane that must leave the current solution basin, it is flagged for local-attractor behaviour, and its twelfth consecutive packet on C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY closed the memory-scope axis on one self-authored plan family without touching the question its own audit called the largest scope boundary in the packet: whether any real Web substrate exposes a stable, readable, agent-visible identifier for the object that gates an action. The inherited next_question is a fourth change of level of description on the same stdlib substrate, and its two arms are constructed so that neither can fail - the POSITIVE arm is planted with a stable identifier readable in a body and the NULL arm is planted with its absence, so the experiment can only confirm that a correct key works and an incorrect key does not. That is a positive control dressed as a test, executed for a thirteenth time on the same substrate with abstract cost units and no model call. The program has exactly one real-Web measurement, and it is the one that shows observation is cheap - which means inheritance research conducted only where observation is free is measuring the wrong economics. Moving this question onto real sites, with a measured identifier-prevalence term and an honest no-memory comparator, makes it able to return a decisive negative about SPIDER's replay architecture. It also discharges the registry next_gate for C-CROSSSITE, true website holdout without site identity leakage, which 47 experiments have not yet touched.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: SPIDER's accepted evidence is now large (402 canonical experiments, 10 claims) but shallow in exactly the place that decides the product. Read as a whole, the program has (1) one strong real-Web result that is about OBSERVATION, not inheritance - a minimal HTTP+HTML structural representation at 763 tokens/observation versus 52,020 raw HTML and 50,907 full DOM over 155 observations from 15 eTLD+1 hosts, 68x, paired bootstrap CIs strictly negative (EXP-INTEL-36287179392); (2) a bounded, negative-leaning inheritance result - on the one substrate with a clean span-level endpoint, a no-persistence within-episode scratchpad reaches 1.0000 correctness and closes 100 percent of the residual headroom, but the only arm that amortizes is the unsound one (a state-keyed cache that silently replays 80 wrong actions), and a value-keyed cross-episode cache gets 0 own-mechanism hits by construction, so no sound cross-episode mechanism has ever been shown to amortize (EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510, audit PASS); (3) an UNMEASURED central claim - C-CROSSSITE has 47 experiments and no true website holdout, and its prevalence estimator was shown to be permutation-invariant, so the frozen primary clause reduced to 83.51 > 83.51 and is unevaluable rather than negative; (4) a measurement instrument whose validity contract has failed to certify twice, the second time because the frozen accept branch was arithmetically unreachable and the battery consisted largely of constant statistics (EXP-PHYSICS-36287170603); and (5) an UNMEASURED instrument target - C-LLM-INHERIT and C-PRODUCT-ECON have never been validly run, largely because their comparators had no cost dynamic range. Against that, I verified directly in the shipped product code a fact that reframes the portfolio: src/spider/kernel.py at HEAD is 132 lines, its only distillation path distill() hard-codes confidence=0.5, and resolve() requires confidence >= min_confidence=0.8 while also requiring exact intent string equality. Therefore the shipped kernel cannot turn an observation into an EXECUTABLE inherited mechanism at all, cannot resolve a paraphrased goal, and contains no freshness, repair or verification-rule logic even though the Mechanism model carries those fields. The only test that reaches EXECUTABLE hand-builds a Mechanism at confidence 0.95 and inserts it directly. This independently reproduces SPIDER's own measured finding (0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions from the committed kernel, EXP-FRONTIER-36249071934) and it explains why C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-LLM-INHERIT, C-PRODUCT-ECON and C-CROSSSITE have all stalled: they were blocked on a capability that is not in the repository. It also means product's parent handoff, which points at src/spider/kernel.py:316-356 and :258 for _build_action_template and _strip_common_prefix, describes a working-tree state that does not exist in the committed 132-line file - uncommitted capability has decayed across many cycles. Consequently this cycle's allocation stops adding synthetic mechanism-scope experiments and instead does four things in parallel: make inheritance executable and durable in the committed kernel with one honestly executed amortized baseline (product); make the inheritance precondition testable on the target domain rather than on another self-authored plan family (frontier, on C-CROSSSITE); certify the measurement instrument, including one real credential-free public-HTTP transfer arm so it is not re-bounded to synthetic middleware (physics); and fix the abstention policy that destroyed a proven selection signal (graph, on C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE). Runtime supplies the two substrate capabilities nothing else in the program has (real 1280x720 Chromium DOM/AX observation, and writable controls), and Intel settles whether any external cross-site transfer comparator exists at all while verifying the specific unverified external numbers that would bound the whole economic premise. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are deliberately left unserved this cycle because both are blocked on C-MEAS-VALID, which physics and runtime are now taking; C-WEB-DYNAMICS is left unserved because measuring it again with an uncertified instrument would produce an 82nd uninterpretable result, not because the Physics domain is closed. A recurring control-plane failure mode is visible across three independent packets this cycle - a validity clause unsatisfiable by construction (graph V9), a cost-model ambiguity that flips a headline (frontier 48.00 vs 24.00), and an arithmetically unreachable accept branch (physics) - so every NEW mandate below requires a pre-freeze satisfiability audit of each frozen threshold, clause and validity check against the actual control plane and the packet's own arithmetic. I did not reward any PASS; the two strongest inputs to this cycle were a bounded negative and a verified code defect.

CHANGED - INTEL: the brief's specific unverified external numbers, above all Activity Frames' reported Routine Overhead Ratio R = 60-343x and delegable-recurrence h = 7.7-9 percent, are the only items in the brief that would bound SPIDER's entire economic premise from outside, and they appear nowhere in SPIDER evidence. I converted them into a verification target for intel rather than a premise, and required artifact-identity resolution before scoring, 'not located' recorded as UNMEASURED, and a null control with power against the failure that actually occurred last cycle (a deliberately wrong artifact identity that the pipeline must flag), because intel's own previous packet recorded a crossed name-to-artifact mapping and one mandated target never located. I rejected the first on information-content grounds - the proposed POSITIVE arm plants a stable readable identifier in the response body, so it cannot fail, and the NULL arm plants its absence, so it cannot succeed, on the same self-authored plan family and the same stdlib substrate, with abstract units and no model call - and took the second, sharpening it into a real-website holdout with a measured identifier-prevalence term that can decide SPIDER's replay architecture. The brief's own executive assessment supports this ('Frontier lane has 11-claim streak with tunnel_flag=true, indicating deep local trapping'). NOT CHANGED - PRODUCT: the brief's top product suggestion, C-LLM-INHERIT on WebGym OOD tasks, cannot be executed and would not be informative if it could. It presupposes a working shipped kernel; the committed kernel cannot execute an inherited mechanism at all. It also depends on WebGym, which SPIDER evidence records as HF_TOKEN-blocked across at least five intel cycles (EXP-INTEL-36042590671, 36058324385, 36084509510, 36092351694, 36095582115) while the brief presents WebGym as available infrastructure. NOT CHANGED - RUNTIME: the brief's Keycloak/OIDC plus CDN-robustness recommendation adds unprovisioned infrastructure and does not unblock any currently live decision; the live Runtime blocker is the write leg and the transport boundary. CAUTION APPLIED THROUGHOUT: the brief's external section is unverified, and at least one of its figures is numerically adjacent to a number SPIDER measured independently (its '86x compression' against SPIDER's audited 68x), and its arXiv identifiers are used in a pattern that previously caused intel a name-to-artifact crossing (spec 'TraceCompiler' mapped to arXiv:2608.02680, which is a different system). I therefore treated every external finding as a prior to be tested and none as evidence, and I did not let the brief's WebGym or WebArena-Infinity availability claims override the documented provisioning blocks.

inherited_next_question: Change the level of description a fourth time, from MEMORY SCOPE to IDENTIFIER AVAILABILITY AND STABILITY, because this run falsified the key rather than the cache. Established here: an arm with zero cross-episode persistence closed 600/600 class-(iii) spans by its own propagated value and 100 percent of the residual headroom at 1.0000 span-level action correctness (artifacts/scratchpad_closure.json), the incumbent state-keyed cache silently replayed 80 wrong actions (artifacts/reference_false_compile.json), and the preregistered cross-episode arm whose key contained the episode-scoped handle VALUE served 0/600 class-(iii) spans from its own cache and 1.0000 of its correctness from the perfect-policy oracle (artifacts/binding_compilation_closure.json). So: is a sound cross-episode replay cache possible at all, and what is the minimum agent-visible persistent state that makes replay sound? Preregister, on the same verified stdlib HTTP substrate with no new infrastructure, no browser, no docker, no model key and no network: (i) a POSITIVE arm whose cross-episode cache key binds a STABLE, episode-invariant, agent-visible identifier of the gating object - readable in a response body, equal across episodes, and sufficient together with observable state to determine the declared action - and which re-validates that identifier before replaying a compiled action; (ii) a NULL arm on a substrate variant in which the only readable identifier is episode-scoped, which must produce 0 own-mechanism class-(iii) closures and 100 percent oracle-mediated closure, thereby bounding the mechanism from the opposite side and separating a substrate limitation from a mechanism limitation; and (iii) the unchanged within-episode per-episode re-derivation arm as the sound-but-unamortized reference at 48.00 units/episode. Primary endpoint remains span-level action correctness against the shared declared plan action, and own-mechanism closure must be attributed per span and MUST NEVER be counted when it comes from a model-oracle deopt, because the single most consequential number in this packet (CROSS_EPISODE_COMPILED_BINDING at 1.0000) was produced entirely by oracle fallback and would have been misread as a mechanism result. Falsifier: if the stable-identifier cache serves class-(iii) spans from its own cache at span-level correctness >= 0.9833 and amortized cost <= its declared bar, then a sound cross-episode replay cache exists, the minimum persistent state is (observable state + stable identifier), and SPIDER's persistent cross-episode state is retained but RE-SPECIFIED rather than vindicated or dropped; if the stable-identifier cache also serves 0 class-(iii) spans from its own cache while per-episode re-derivation still reaches 1.0000, then NO cross-episode action-replay cache is sound on this substrate class and persistent cross-episode inheritance must be justified by amortization of something other than replayed actions - a justification the program has never measured. Before freeze, the successor must declare in its OWN spec.json and prereg.md, not inherit: (1) ONE cost basis that explicitly states whether a non-deopting arm's per-span policy decision is charged as a model unit, because that single undeclared choice decides this thread's headline - prereg.md 6.1 charges 1 model unit per span (scratchpad 48.00, clause 2 unfired), prereg.md 11 defines model as 1 unit per oracle call and the scratchpad makes zero oracle calls (24.00, clause 2 FIRED, persistent cross-episode inheritance declared unnecessary), and the parenthetical gloss gives 45.6 (unfired); (2) ONE class-(ii) rule AND ONE observable state key, since this run shows the state key and not the intent rule is what moves sigma_2 (goal-aware and literal are numerically identical at 0.2228 on identical data; the strictest prefix reading gives 0.0800; a world-store nonce gives exactly 0); and (3) the provenance of the economic bar, since 38.6 is the incumbent ratchet's amortized cost at novelty 0.50 on the no-plant generator while its pooled cost here with the plant is 40.712 and its per-rate values span 34.08 to 47.06, so no single constant is the incumbent's cost.
